messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: P1 - spike in 5xx + gateway timeouts on /v1/chat/completions. Start ~1845788900, current error rate 22% (normal ~0.3%). Top symptoms: 502 Bad Gateway, 504 upstream timeout, 'proto parse error' from prefix-kv-read. Pager: @maria (oncall)
maria (oncall): ack. grabbing context. creating this thread for live triage. attaching initial alert graphs.
ryan (eng-runtime): joining. traces show runtime failing when resolving prefixes: prefix_cache.lookup -> shard.read -> proto_parse_error. Stack: prefix_cache::read -> kv_client::read_segment -> proto::deserialize.
nina (eng-platform): infra side: prefix-cache fleet reports surge in evictions (~10x) and high disk ops on nodes pcache-eu-*. Network retransmit small but consistent. Some nodes reporting tmpfs exhaustion.
chris (sre): logs show "unexpected EOF while parsing protobuf" and "write offset larger than file size" on several shard files. Looks like partial/fragmented writes.
lila (support): customer impact: multiple customers report high failure rates for chat and embeddings. Two enterprise customers opened Priority tickets. Latency for affected requests jumped to 3-6s then 5xx.
rachel (customer-success): I'm pinging top impacted customers (omega-analytics, finapps-inc) to say we’re investigating; offering interim callbacks.
maria (oncall): immediate mitigations proposal: A) route around pcache (force origin reads) B) scale pcache nodes up and rebalance C) set eviction throttle D) take compaction offline. Prefer safe path: route origin reads for all namespaces hitting parse errors while we investigate.
ryan (eng-runtime): we have a dynamic flag prefix_cache.enabled that can be tuned per-region. I can flip reads -> passthrough for affected region quickly. Also will add immediate read-side checksum guard so parse errors are treated as cache miss.
nina (eng-platform): prepping config push:
```yaml
dynamic_flags:
  prefix_cache:
    read_passthrough_regions: ["eu-west-1"]
    global_read_enabled: true
```
Canary to 5% traffic then roll.
chris (sre): before we flip, dump corrupted shard metadata for forensics: running pcache_inspect to extract entries with parse failures and saving to s3. I'll include node ids and file offsets.
maria (oncall): go ahead. I'll initiate canary after we have sample batch. Also increasing gateway idle timeout 9s -> 18s for /v1/chat/completions to reduce client timeouts during fallback.
incident-bot: Config deploy started: dynamic_flags v7 -> canary 5%.
maria (oncall): canary green for 5% — error rate in canary dropped to 2.5%. Rolling to 25%. Observed traces show origin_kv read latencies up ~120ms but success.
ryan (eng-runtime): sample trace (canary):
```
trace_id=tr-99a1
step1: prefix_cache.checksum -> mismatch -> treat as miss -> origin_kv.get -> OK
latency: 280ms
```
nina (eng-platform): rolling to 100% now. dynamic_flags v7 applied.
incident-bot: dynamic_flags v7 active on 100% traffic.
maria (oncall): monitoring: error rate fell from 22% -> 1.6% within 8 minutes. p95 latency increased ~150ms. Good sign.
rachel (customer-success): notifying customers: sent interim update to omega-analytics and finapps-inc with mitigation steps and ETA for root cause.
lila (support): creating consolidated ticket and attaching initial dumps.
chris (sre): dump complete: s3://redwood-incidents/1845789012/corrupt-metadata.tar.gz includes ~2.8k entries. early look: many entries are zero-length footers and truncated segment frames.
ryan (eng-runtime): quick tail analysis: truncated frames line up with recent compaction windows on certain shards. Hypothesis: compaction writes are not atomic; under I/O pressure partial files are visible to readers. Combined with eviction thrash and process restarts (OOM kills) this yields corrupted reads. Also noticed compaction scheduled on same timeframe as kernel patch rollout to some cache hosts.
nina (eng-platform): verifying node events: pcache-eu-3/4/5 had reboots last night due to unattended kernel updates and later experienced memory pressure. Also compaction started subsequently.
maria (oncall): plan for full remediation: 1) keep read_passthrough in place until nodes repaired 2) pause compaction cluster-wide 3) schedule rolling drain+fsck+restart for affected nodes 4) implement read-repair fallback for checksum mismatch 5) add eviction throttling to avoid storms. Assign owners.
chris (sre): I'll coordinate node drains and fsck. recommended sequence: mark node maintenance, wait for clients to fallback, run fsck/repair, restore from healthy peer snapshot if needed, rejoin.
nina (eng-platform): pausing compaction via flag compaction.enabled=false and enabling eviction_throttle.enabled=true. Pushing now.
incident-bot: compaction.disabled, eviction_throttle.enabled flags applied. Maintenance window scheduled: 1845790200 - 1845797400.
maria (oncall): ryan — can you ship a hotfix to treat proto parse exceptions as cache miss (no 5xx), and emit telemetry for read-repair?
ryan (eng-runtime): yes. small change: wrap deserialization, on error increment metric prefix_cache.deserialize_failures and fallback to origin_kv.get. PR reviewed, merging to runtime hotfix branch and deploying to API fleet.
chris (sre): first node drained and restarted; fsck found truncated segment files; replaced with replica snapshot and node rejoined healthy. Repeating for next nodes.
maria (oncall): after node 1 restart and compaction pause + hotfix + read_passthrough we see baseline restored: error rate ~0.4% (normal). Will keep monitoring for 30m.
rachel (customer-success): sending follow-up update to customers with timeline and mitigation summary. scheduling post-incident call for major impacted customers.
lila (support): tickets updated with incident id INC-2024-1845789012 and artifacts attached.
chris (sre): all affected nodes restarted safely. compaction remains disabled until engineering PR to make compaction atomic lands. We'll also set eviction throttle defaults higher.
ryan (eng-runtime): followups: implement read-repair (verify checksum on write and read, automatic fallback + async repair), add instrumentation to detect partial-write patterns, add feature flag for atomic compaction stepping.
nina (eng-platform): infra followups: change kernel rollout policy to staggered batches with memory-pressure checks, ensure tmpfs thresholds and limit compaction concurrency per node.
maria (oncall): handing off to nina for remediation and postmortem. Thanks team. Closing page. :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: Page closed. Incident recorded: incident_id=INC-2024-1845789012. Please file postmortem within 3 business days.
rachel (customer-success): scheduled post-incident customer debrief for next Wed.
lila (support): marking all impacted tickets as incident-linked.
chris (sre): short list for postmortem: root cause: non-atomic compaction writes + kernel reboots causing partial files + eviction storms; mitigations performed: read_passthrough, hotfix deserialize-fallback, compaction disabled, node drains+fsck, eviction throttle; action items: atomic compaction, write-checksum on write, read-repair autoshadow, safer kernel rollout, tougher eviction controls.
ryan (eng-runtime): arch note: will propose compaction redesign to use write-rename-atomic pattern and add a compaction job lock.
nina (eng-platform): uploading logs/traces to s3://redwood-incidents/1845789012/artifacts.tar.gz and will own the postmortem doc. Thanks everyone.
